title: CIOMS Working Group XIV on AI in Pharmacovigilance
answer: CIOMS Working Group XIV brought regulators and industry together to set principles for AI in pharmacovigilance. Its report treats AI tools that influence patient safety as needing governance close to that applied to medicines themselves: risk based validation, human oversight, transparency and continuous monitoring.

reading.body:
CIOMS Working Group XIV set principles for AI in pharmacovigilance, treating tools that affect patient safety as needing governance close to that of medicines.

The pattern is that governance arrived before deployment. Regulators and industry wrote the rules together, and the resulting framework is risk based validation, human oversight, transparency and continuous monitoring. That is the same posture applied to medicines themselves, which means an AI tool that touches a safety decision is not treated as ordinary software.

For AI specifically, this matters because pharmacovigilance is a domain where an error can harm patients directly, so the tolerance for unvalidated models is low. The guidance gives a safety team a backbone for policy rather than a blank page.

What the data does not cover is the substance of the report itself. It names the principles but not the thresholds, the validation methods, or how any of it is enforced. It also says nothing about the compute, buildings, or power behind these tools, and nothing here supports a claim about them.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.
The 2026 package of targeted amendments to the EU AI Act, deferring high-risk deadlines and restructuring conformity assessment.

The requirement that a person can understand, intervene in, and override AI decisions. Mandated for high-risk uses under the EU AI Act, and only real when the human has the time, information, and authority to actually intervene.

explainer:
The Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences is an international body that brings regulators, industry and academics together to write consensus guidance on drug safety and research. Its working group reports, for example on safety reporting and benefit risk, have shaped regulatory practice worldwide for decades.

Working Group XIV addressed artificial intelligence in pharmacovigilance. Its report covers how to decide where AI is appropriate, how to validate and monitor AI tools, what human oversight is needed, how to manage transparency and explainability, and how to handle data privacy and fairness. Because regulators helped write it, it gives companies a widely recognised basis for their own policies and a common language for inspection discussions.
